stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $Y \subset X$ be an irreducible closed subset.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset such that $Y \cap U$ is nonempty.
Then
$$
\text{codim}(Y, X) = \text{codim}(Y \cap U, U)
$$
hypotheses:
Let $X$ be a topological space.
Let $Y \subset X$ be an irreducible closed subset.
Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset such that $Y \cap U$ is nonempty.

reason: Closure and intersection with the open subspace give an inclusion-preserving bijection of irreducible closed subsets meeting the open, preserving maximal chain lengths and codimensions.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is catenary,
\item $X$ has an open covering by catenary spaces.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, in this case any locally closed subspace of $X$ is catenary.

reason: The source only treats restriction from a catenary space to an open subset, then says details omitted. The converse from an open cover to global catenarity and the locally closed conclusion are not actually proved here.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is catenary, and
\item for every pair of irreducible closed subsets $Y \subset Y'$ we have
$\text{codim}(Y, Y') < \infty$ and for every triple
$Y \subset Y' \subset Y''$ of irreducible closed subsets we have
$$
\text{codim}(Y, Y'') = \text{codim}(Y, Y') + \text{codim}(Y', Y'').
$$
\end{enumerate}
conclusions:
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is catenary, and
\item for every pair of irreducible closed subsets $Y \subset Y'$ we have
$\text{codim}(Y, Y') < \infty$ and for every triple
$Y \subset Y' \subset Y''$ of irreducible closed subsets we have
$$
\text{codim}(Y, Y'') = \text{codim}(Y, Y') + \text{codim}(Y', Y'').
$$
\end{enumerate}

reason: Catenarity implies additivity by concatenating maximal chains; conversely, codimension additivity along a maximal chain forces equal finite lengths.
